title: Continuity protocol for segmented stream delivery and client rejoin handling
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Customers rely on long-lived streaming responses for multi-step tool/function-calling workflows and structured JSON outputs. Existing behavior can produce partial JSON blocks, ambiguous boundaries, and poor client experience when a connection drops mid-output. This ticket specifies a continuity protocol that enables: 1) deterministic rejoin semantics so clients can request only missing output; 2) unambiguous segment boundaries for structured outputs (tool calls / JSON blocks); and 3) a compatibility shim for legacy newline-delimited and minimal-SSE clients.

Goals: 
- Define server markers (sequence anchors) and idempotent fragment ids to allow minimal replay/backfill.
- Ensure function-call frames are atomic from the client's point-of-view (either delivered fully or signaled as streaming-in-progress with a rejoin strategy).
- Support structured output modes: JSONL, nested-toolcall frames, and server-declared schema bundles.
- Provide a negotiate-header flow so older clients are not regressed.

Non-goals: 
- Full redesign of client SDKs in this ticket (we will publish an SDK compatibility guide and small helper patch later).

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Server emits a stable sequence_anchor header per connection and per emitted segment: e.g., "anchor: s-<stream-id>-<offset>".
2) Each chunk contains a single top-level fragment metadata line preceding payload, formatted as: "fragment: <fragment-id> offset=<byte-offset> atomic=<true|false>".
3) Atomic=true is required for tool/function-call frames; server must not split an atomic fragment across different fragment-ids.
4) A client reconnect request can supply last_seen_fragment=<id> and optionally last_byte_offset=<n> to request incremental backfill.
5) A compatibility negotiation header "X-Redwood-Stream: v2" must be supported; if absent, server falls back to the legacy newline-delimited JSON streaming with a best-effort resume using last newline boundary.
6) End-to-end integration tests (automated harness) covering: clean close, mid-atomic-fragment drop and rejoin, multi-toolcall sequence with interleaved non-atomic tokens, and legacy client fallback.

Design notes and trade-offs: 
- Sequence anchors vs tokens: we choose human-readable anchors tied to stream-id+offset (instead of opaque tokens) to simplify debugging and allow operator-level reconciliation across logs. This increases header length but aids post-mortem.
- Atomic fragments for tool calls: enforcing atomic fragments reduces server compression/batching opportunities. To mitigate cost, we allow non-atomic fragments for plain text tokens and recommend batching threshold heuristics (max 4KB or 50 tokens) before emitting a fragment boundary.
- Backfill strategy: server will attempt byte-level backfill if last_byte_offset provided, otherwise fall back to last_fragment-id re-emit. Byte-level resumes are best-effort and only supported when the client previously negotiated "resume=byte" capability.
- Reconciliation vs duplication: on reconnect we may re-send up to the last atomic fragment to guarantee client has a complete toolcall. Clients must deduplicate by fragment-id. We will publish a client helper that performs idempotent application.
- Compatibility shim: legacy clients expecting JSONL will receive a legacy-mode stream where each event is newline-delimited JSON and the server inserts simple resume markers as comments ("#resume:<anchor>") between lines. This is lossy for byte-level resumes but better than dropping the feature.

Protocol examples (literal): 
- Initial connect (headers): 
  GET /v1/chat/stream HTTP/1.1
  Host: api.redwood.ai
  X-Redwood-Stream: v2
  Accept: text/event-stream
  Authorization: Bearer <key>

- Server first lines: 
  anchor: s-76a4-0
  fragment: f-76a4-1 offset=0 atomic=false
  data: {"role":"assistant","delta":"Here's the plan:"}

- Tool call atomic fragment: 
  fragment: f-76a4-2 offset=128 atomic=true
  data: {"tool_call":{"name":"search","args":{"q":"redwood streaming guide"}}}

- Reconnect request (client): 
  GET /v1/chat/stream?last_seen_fragment=f-76a4-1&last_byte_offset=124 HTTP/1.1
  X-Redwood-Stream: v2

Edge cases and open questions: 
- How to handle partial multi-byte UTF-8 characters at chunk boundaries? We will ensure fragment boundaries align on Unicode codepoint boundaries; runtime may need to buffer until codepoint complete.
- What to do when a toolcall result is large (>> 8KB)? Plan: server may mark the toolcall fragment as atomic but internally stream compressed sub-chunks with a secondary sub-sequence that is always re-assembled server-side before re-emitting to clients as a single atomic fragment. This is a performance optimization and will be behind a feature flag.
- Security: fragment ids should be unguessable within a stream but we avoid global leakage. Anchors contain stream-id but not customer identifiers.

Links: 
- Confluence spec (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Stream+Continuity+Spec+v2 
- PR with preliminary framing parser: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 
- Test harness: https://gitlab.redwood.ai/infra/stream-test-harness/-/tree/feature/continuity

Next steps: 
- Merge runtime framing parser PR and enable v2 behind a feature flag in staging. (ENG owner: Dmitri)
- Publish SDK helper for fragment dedupe and reconnect semantics (small patch in SDK repo).
- Run canary with 10% of hosted traffic and measure duplicate-fragment rate, reconnection success rate, and per-request added header overhead.

Metrics to track: 
- reconnect_success_rate (target >= 99.5% for intermittent disconnects)
- duplicate_fragment_apply_rate (goal < 0.1% after helper adoption)
- avg_resume_bytes_sent (should be << full-response size for long streams)
